rule.description: A function or method whose parameter list decomposes one logical value -- the reply endpoint of a cluster peer (its address, port and node name) -- into separate sibling scalar parameters. The repository already models that value with bundled types (net.UDPAddr, net.IP, memberlist.Address, and the query/relay message structs); a signature that instead repeats the traveling address/port/name group as siblings is the data clump.

checks.description: Detect callables in the serf core that accept the peer reply endpoint -- network address, port number and node name -- as separate sibling parameters. A parameter is classified by identifier tokens plus its declared type: an address slot is an address/address/ip-named slice-of-byte or net.IP parameter, a port slot is a port-named integer parameter, and a name slot is a name/node-named string parameter. All three slots must appear among the same callable's sibling parameters for a match; identifiers are tokenized on camel humps and underscores so clock terms such as LamportTime are not mistaken for ports.
checks.detected_relation: peer reply destination (address, port, node name) -> decomposed into separate sibling parameters of one callable
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The three values always describe one logical destination -- where to send or join this peer. The codebase already carries that value bundled in net.UDPAddr, memberlist.Address and the query/relay message structs; accepting the three members as siblings repeats the traveling group at every hop of a call chain, forces representation and width conversions between hops, and makes every endpoint-affecting change touch every signature along the chain.

excluded.reason: The wire message struct already bundles the reply endpoint as struct fields (address bytes, port, source node); struct field definitions are the bundled form the rule points to, not the flagged sibling-parameter form.
The relay header carries its destination as a bundled net.UDPAddr field plus a destination name field; the rule flags decomposed parameter lists, not already-bundled message fields.

The client-facing query event stores its reply endpoint as three struct fields accessed only through the type itself; a struct is a bundled owner, and the exposed event surface must stay stable, so the rule deliberately does not flag field definitions.
Intent messages carry a single node name string with no address/port siblings; a partial group is outside the traveling reply-destination relation.
Clock parameters such as queryLTime or ltime tokenize to 'lamport'+'time' and are excluded by the token-based slot classification, so clock plumbing is never counted as a port slot.
